newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian money market rates level, demand lively.
newsitem.headline: Croatian money market rates level, demand lively.

text.p: Croatian money market rates were unchanged in somewhat livelier trade as demand for kuna funds increased on Friday.
"There were no problems today although Friday is usually a difficult day due to various payments. There was enough money on offer," one dealer said.
She said the supply shrank from Thursday but was still satisfactory and some 25 million kuna were left in surplus.
The banking sector had 100.2 million kuna in outstanding central bank Lombard loans on Thursday evening, and no new laons were sought on Friday, an official told Reuters.
Demand of 28 million kuna was met in full. Call money accounted for most of the trade and was granted at a steady 10.5 percent.
Term loans ranged between 11 percent for one-week funds and 18 percent for one-month borrowings.

Overnight trade on Friday totalled 22.2 million kuna after one bank sought 1.2 million to cover a shortfall. Another 21 million went to two banks and one savings bank for maintaining their mandatory reserves. -- Laura Lui, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
